title: PollBehavior.Manual registers a remote without a timer; pulls happen only via triggerPull
content:
`PollBehavior` is set per remote in `RemoteOptions` and controls only the schedule, never whether the channel connects:

```typescript
enum PollBehavior { Auto = "auto", Manual = "manual" }
```

`Auto` is the default. The channel runs its interval timer in the background: **the first tick fires immediately on `init()`**, then repeats every `pollIntervalMs` (default 2000 ms). That immediate first tick matters — adding an `Auto` remote produces a fetch straight away, not after one interval.

`Manual` still registers and connects the channel; it simply never ticks on its own. Pulls happen only when you ask:

```typescript
triggerPull(name: string): void;
```

`triggerPull` runs exactly one pull cycle. For a `Manual` remote it does **not** promote it to recurring polling — the remote stays `Manual` and a single fetch runs. This makes `Manual` the right choice for test harnesses, on-demand refresh buttons, and any environment where you want deterministic control over when network traffic happens.

Two edge behaviors: `triggerPull` on an unknown remote throws ``Remote with name '${name}' does not exist``, and on a `GqlResponseChannel` (the Switchboard push side) it is a **no-op**, because that channel has nothing to poll.

Polling is not a naive timer. Two mechanisms guard the reactor:

- **Backpressure** — a tick *defers* when the reactor queue depth exceeds `maxQueueDepth` (default 100) and rechecks after `backpressureCheckIntervalMs` (default 500 ms). A saturated reactor stops pulling more work onto itself rather than piling it up. This is why `GqlRequestChannelFactory` needs the queue passed to its constructor.
- **Exponential backoff** — transient poll failures retry between `retryBaseDelayMs` (default 1000) and `retryMaxDelayMs` (default 300000, i.e. five minutes).

All four are optional `parameters` on the `"gql"` channel config alongside the required `url`, and each is type-checked at registration: a wrong type throws, for example `'"pollIntervalMs" parameter must be a number'`.

_Source: apps/academy/docs/academy/04-Reference/01-Reactor/04-Synchronization.md (Powerhouse v6.2.2-dev.45)._
